title: Getting around Prague
summary: How Prague's metro, trams, buses, trains, ferries and night lines fit together; tickets, validation and inspectors; and all the Czech you'll read and hear on the way.

phrasebook.title: Metro announcements
phrasebook.intro: The recorded voices you'll hear on every journey.

phrases.en: Please finish getting on and off, the doors are closing.
phrases.note: Every time the doors close. Step back.
Press the button (or raise your hand at the stop).

practice.title: Announcements and signs
practice.description: Understand what you hear and read on the network.

exercises.prompt: Ukončete, prosím, výstup a nástup, dveře se zavírají.
answers: Please {finish|stop} {getting on and off|getting off and on|boarding and exiting|exiting and boarding}[,] the doors are closing[.]
{Stand clear|Stop boarding}[,] the doors are closing[.]
exercises.why: výstup = getting off, nástup = getting on, dveře se zavírají = the doors are closing.

exercises.prompt: Konečná stanice. Prosíme, vystupte.
answers: This is the {terminus|end of the line}[.] Please {get off|exit|leave the train}[.]
exercises.why: konečná = terminus, vystupte = get off (vy imperative of vystoupit).

exercises.prompt: Přestup na linku C.
exercises.why: přestup = change, transfer.

exercises.prompt: You hear **"Zastávka na znamení."** What do you have to do if you want to get off?
exercises.why: zastávka na znamení = request stop: the tram or bus only stops if someone presses the button (or waits at the stop with a raised hand).

hints.explain: At a request stop the vehicle won't stop unless you press the button.

exercises.prompt: Which sign do you follow to get out of the metro to the street? Type the Czech word.
exercises.why: Výstup = exit. Vstup / vchod = entrance; přestup = change to another line.

hints.explain: Přestup means changing to another line. The way out is Výstup.
Vstup is the entrance. The way out is Výstup.

exercises.prompt: A yellow poster at your stop says **výluka**. What does it mean?
exercises.why: výluka = a planned closure or diversion; náhradní doprava = the replacement service.

exercises.prompt: During a closure, what is the replacement service called? Type the two Czech words.
exercises.why: náhradní doprava = replacement transport, usually buses marked X.

exercises.prompt: An electronic board says **"za 4 min"**. When does the tram leave?
exercises.why: za + time = in (time from now): za 4 minuty, za hodinu.

exercises.cs: Ukončete, prosím, výstup a nástup, dveře se zavírají.
exercises.en: Please finish getting on and off, the doors are closing.
answers: Ukončete[,] prosím[,] výstup a nástup[,] dveře se zavírají
exercises.why: The metro door announcement: ukončete (finish) … výstup a nástup (getting off and on), dveře se zavírají (the doors are closing).

exercises.prompt: You're on Line A. What can you do at the next station?
exercises.why: Přestup na linku B: change to line B. Přestup is a transfer; na linku is na + accusative (where to).

exercises.prompt: Where does this sign send you?
exercises.why: Výstup is the exit (literally "getting out"). Its opposite at the platform is nástup, getting on.

practice.title: Know the network
practice.description: Lines, colours and the key stations.

exercises.prompt: Which metro line is **yellow**? (A, B or C)
exercises.why: A is green, B is yellow, C is red.

exercises.prompt: Which metro line is **red**? (A, B or C)
exercises.why: A is green, B is yellow, C is red.

exercises.prompt: At which station can you change between lines **A and B**?
exercises.why: Můstek (A/B), Muzeum (A/C), Florenc (B/C).

hints.explain: Muzeum connects A and C. A and B meet at Můstek.
Florenc connects B and C. A and B meet at Můstek.

exercises.prompt: At which station can you change between lines **A and C**?
exercises.why: Muzeum (A/C), Můstek (A/B), Florenc (B/C).

hints.explain: Můstek connects A and B. A and C meet at Muzeum.

exercises.prompt: At which station can you change between lines **B and C**?
exercises.why: Florenc (B/C), Můstek (A/B), Muzeum (A/C).

exercises.prompt: Night trams have numbers in which range?
exercises.why: Night trams are 91–99 and all meet at Lazarská; night buses are 901–915.

exercises.prompt: Which trolleybus connects the airport with metro line A (Nádraží Veleslavín)?
exercises.why: Trolleybus 59 (it replaced bus 119). Bus 100 goes to Zličín on line B; night bus 910 runs when the metro is closed.

hints.explain: Bus 119 no longer runs: trolleybus 59 replaced it.

exercises.prompt: You have a **paper** ticket. Where do you validate it before taking the metro?
answers: at the top of the escalators
exercises.why: In the metro, validate at the entrance to the platforms, before the escalators. On trams and buses, validate on board.

practice.title: Asking your way
practice.description: Questions to ask on the move, and the station-name endings that go with them.

exercises.prompt: Does this tram go to Anděl?
exercises.why: Vehicles use jet (jede), not jít. Destinations that are stations usually take na + accusative: na Anděl.

hints.explain: Vehicles "ride" in Czech: jede, not jde.
Prague stations usually take na: na Anděl.

exercises.prompt: Are you getting off? (to a stranger)
exercises.why: Vystupujete? (vy form). The classic question before your stop when someone is between you and the door.

hints.explain: That's the ty form. To a stranger, use vy: Vystupujete?

exercises.prompt: Where can I buy a ticket?
exercises.why: koupit + accusative: jízdenka → jízdenku (lístek doesn't change).

hints.explain: jízdenka is the object of koupit: accusative jízdenku.

exercises.prompt: One 90-minute ticket, please.
answers: Jednu jízdenku na devadesát minut[, prosím].
Jeden lístek na devadesát minut[, prosím].
exercises.why: jízdenka na devadesát minut ("a ticket for ninety minutes"), in the accusative because you're asking for it: jednu jízdenku.

hints.wrong: Jedna jízdenka na devadesát minut[, prosím].
hints.explain: You're asking for it, so use the accusative: jednu jízdenku.

exercises.prompt: Which stop should I get off at?
exercises.why: na + locative: na které zastávce (zastávka → zastávce). mít + infinitive = "should".

hints.explain: na (at a place) takes the locative: na které zastávce.

exercises.prompt: Vystupuju na Můstk___.
exercises.why: Station names decline. na + locative: Můstek → na Můstku (the e drops out, like Marek → Marka).

hints.explain: Masculine nouns ending in -k take -u in the locative: na Můstku.

exercises.prompt: Přestupuju na Florenc___.
exercises.why: Florenc is a soft feminine noun (like píseň), so the locative ends in -i: na Florenci.

hints.explain: Florenc is feminine and soft: na Florenci, not -u.
Florenc is a soft feminine noun: the locative is -i, na Florenci.

context.speaker: Revizor
context.cs: Dobrý den, přepravní kontrola. Vaše jízdenky, prosím.
context.en: Hello, ticket inspection. Your tickets, please.

exercises.prompt: Say: here it is, I have it in the app.
answers: [{Dobrý den|Prosím}[,] ]{Tady je|Tady|Tady ji máte|Tady máte|Prosím}[,] mám ji v aplikaci[.]
exercises.why: mám ji v aplikaci: ji refers back to jízdenka (feminine accusative); v + locative: aplikace → v aplikaci.

hints.wrong: [{Dobrý den|Prosím}[,] ]{Tady je|Tady|Tady máte|Prosím}[,] mám ho v aplikaci[.]
hints.explain: jízdenka is feminine, so "it" is ji: mám ji v aplikaci.

hints.wrong: [{Dobrý den|Prosím}[,] ]{Tady je|Tady|Tady máte|Prosím}[,] mám ji v aplikace[.]
